nodes.title: Communication Systems
nodes.summary: This section presents the communication systems component of avionics, focusing on VHF communication, its assigned frequency range (118‑137 MHz AM voice) and the line‑of‑sight nature of its propagation.
objectives: Describe the role of communication systems in avionics
List the VHF frequency band used for voice communications
Explain why VHF communication is limited to line‑of‑sight

nodes.title: Summary
nodes.summary: The summary section reviews the key points of the communication systems lesson, emphasizing that VHF is used for line‑of‑sight operations while HF is used for long‑range oceanic communications.
objectives: Summarize the main concepts of aviation communication systems
Differentiate between VHF line‑of‑sight and HF oceanic usage

nodes.title: Review Questions
nodes.summary: This section provides review questions to assess learners’ understanding of VHF and HF usage within aviation communication, reinforcing the concepts covered earlier.
objectives: Answer questions about the VHF frequency band
Explain why HF is preferred for oceanic communications

nodes.title: Navigation Systems
nodes.summary: This section introduces navigation systems used in aviation, focusing on VOR (VHF Omnidirectional Range) and DME (Distance Measuring Equipment). It explains that VOR provides bearing information while DME supplies slant‑range distance.
objectives: Identify the purpose of VOR and DME in navigation
Describe how DME measures slant range

nodes.title: Summary
nodes.summary: The summary consolidates the key points of the navigation topic, emphasizing that the combination of VOR and DME allows a position fix and that GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) can augment these traditional aids.
objectives: Summarize how VOR and DME together determine position
Recognize GNSS as an augmenting navigation system

properties.text:
Communication Systems

This section presents the communication systems component of avionics, focusing on VHF communication, its assigned frequency range (118‑137 MHz AM voice) and the line‑of‑sight nature of its propagation.

Objectives:
- Describe the role of communication systems in avionics
- List the VHF frequency band used for voice communications
- Explain why VHF communication is limited to line‑of‑sight
properties.heading: Communication Systems

properties.text:
Summary

The summary section reviews the key points of the communication systems lesson, emphasizing that VHF is used for line‑of‑sight operations while HF is used for long‑range oceanic communications.

Objectives:
- Summarize the main concepts of aviation communication systems
- Differentiate between VHF line‑of‑sight and HF oceanic usage
properties.heading: Summary

properties.text:
Review Questions

This section provides review questions to assess learners’ understanding of VHF and HF usage within aviation communication, reinforcing the concepts covered earlier.

Objectives:
- Answer questions about the VHF frequency band
- Explain why HF is preferred for oceanic communications
properties.heading: Review Questions

properties.text:
Navigation Systems

This section introduces navigation systems used in aviation, focusing on VOR (VHF Omnidirectional Range) and DME (Distance Measuring Equipment). It explains that VOR provides bearing information while DME supplies slant‑range distance.

Objectives:
- Identify the purpose of VOR and DME in navigation
- Explain how VOR gives bearing
- Describe how DME measures slant range
properties.heading: Navigation Systems

properties.text:
Summary

The summary consolidates the key points of the navigation topic, emphasizing that the combination of VOR and DME allows a position fix and that GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) can augment these traditional aids.

Objectives:
- Summarize how VOR and DME together determine position
- Recognize GNSS as an augmenting navigation system
properties.heading: Summary

properties.text:
Review Questions

This section provides review questions to test the learner’s understanding of DME’s measurement and the concept of slant range.

Objectives:
- Answer what DME measures
- Define slant range
